# vendored-from: alexandrapaiz/alexandra-systems tools/secret-print-baseline.txt @ 08ba7f5
# vendored-from: do not edit here except to add this repository's own
# vendored-from: accepted findings. Re-vendor with HQ's tools/install-secret-hook.py.
#
# Accepted L-X5 findings — tools/check-secret-print.py --baseline
#
# Every line below is a finding the checker is right about and that this
# repository has decided to keep, with the reason. A finding that is not here
# and not suppressed by an inline `L-X5-ALLOW` marker fails the check, which
# is the point: this file is short and reviewed, and growing it is a decision
# someone has to write down.
#
# Format: path | CODE | the source line's own text.
# Line numbers are deliberately absent, so an edit above a finding does not
# silently retire its exemption.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# URSA'S OWN DIRECTIVES, AND WHY THEY ARE COMMENTS
#
# Two directives below are read by `tools/secret-print-exemptions.py`, Ursa's
# gate over this file. They are written as comments on purpose: HQ's
# `load_baseline()` skips every line starting with `#` and splits an entry on
# only its first two `|`, so a fourth field would change the format this file
# is vendored in, and a comment cannot. Re-vendoring drops them, and the gate
# then says they are missing rather than passing without them.
#
#   # review-by: YYYY-MM-DD
#       On the line DIRECTLY ABOVE a `path | CODE | text` entry, and dating
#       that one entry only. No inheritance down a block: an entry appended
#       under another entry's argument would otherwise be exempt on
#       somebody else's reasoning. Past the date, the gate exits 1 and the
#       entry costs a fresh argument or a new date, which is the price this
#       file exists to charge. There is no "never": an exemption that cannot
#       expire is the dangerous half of this whole mechanism, because the
#       condition it was accepted under is exactly the thing nobody re-reads.
#
#   # specimen-file: <exact path> | <reason>
#       A file whose SUBJECT is defective lines, so that every finding in it
#       is a fixture rather than a defect. These carry no date, and that
#       asymmetry is argued rather than assumed: no future event could make
#       a lint's own test corpus stop needing to contain the shapes the lint
#       detects, so a date on one would come due and be extended unread,
#       which is worse than no date. What replaces the date is confinement
#       and staleness. The path is exact, never a glob, so each one is an
#       individual decision; and a declared file holding no suppressed
#       finding is exit 1, so the declaration cannot outlive its subject.
#       Ursa's exo seat hit the same shape on 2026-11-09 from the other
#       side and moved its lint's corpus out of source into data; this is
#       the case where the corpus is HQ's file and cannot be moved.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The standard GitHub Actions masking idiom, generated into every
# `agent-<seat>.yml` workflow in this repository (first found when the
# checker itself was installed, 2026-11-02): `auth` carries a base64
# Langfuse basic-auth header and these two lines are the only way to
# register a value for masking or hand it to the next step inside Actions.
# No seat token may write under `.github/workflows/` in this repository
# (pm.md §9, "workflow files belong to HQ"), so neither line is this
# repository's to fix even though the checker is right that they print a
# secret; the fix, if one exists, is HQ's across every product at once.
# HQ's own `tools/secret-print-baseline.txt` accepts the identical two
# lines for the identical reason, which is where this entry was copied
# from.
#
# review-by 2027-02-15, which is a security run date and not a round number.
# What to ask then: has HQ changed the generator, and is `::add-mask::` still
# the only way to register a value for masking inside Actions? If either has
# moved, this entry is the thing that was holding the old answer.
# review-by: 2027-02-15
.github/workflows/agent-*.yml | X5-PRINT | echo "::add-mask::$auth"
# review-by: 2027-02-15
.github/workflows/agent-*.yml | X5-PRINT | echo "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS=Authorization=Basic $auth" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The vendored test suite is a corpus of the shapes the checker detects, so
# every one of its fixture strings is, by construction, a line that trips the
# scan. Ten of them do, each carrying its own inline `L-X5-ALLOW` marker with
# a reason. The file is HQ's and says "do not edit here", so the corpus
# cannot be moved into data the way a corpus of ours would be; declaring the
# file is the honest alternative to the gate silently not counting markers.
# specimen-file: tools/tests/test_secret_print.py | HQ's vendored suite for the checker: every fixture is a specimen of a shape the checker is supposed to find
